title: Quantum Imaginary Time Evolution on an Infinite 1D Chain
authors: Hao-Ti Hung, Tung Tsao, Ying-Jer Kao
abstract: We introduce a quantum-circuit algorithm for performing imaginary-time evolution on infinite one-dimensional lattice systems. The method uses a parameterized quantum circuit to represent a uniform matrix product state ansatz. We derive the ITE algorithm using the time-dependent variational principle and employ the quantum Lanczos algorithm to improve the ground-state energy estimate. As a benchmark, we simulate the transverse-field Ising model using both classical simulators and IBM Quantum devices. Our analysis includes a statistical study of the distributions of the cost function and energy density obtained from quantum measurements, illustrating the effects of finite-sampling noise on convergence.
summary: This work introduces a quantum-circuit algorithm to simulate imaginary-time evolution on infinite 1D quantum chains, crucial for finding ground-state energies. It details using the Time-Dependent Variational Principle mapped onto quantum circuits and refines the results using the quantum Lanczos algorithm. Furthermore, the paper provides a deep statistical analysis of noise sources encountered when estimating energy via quantum measurements.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of performing imaginary-time evolution (ITE) on infinite 1D quantum lattice systems using quantum circuits.
main_result: The quantum Lanczos algorithm provides a robust method to estimate the ground-state energy, outperforming simple unitary approximations, while statistical analysis reveals complex noise sources in optimization landscapes.
method: The core method adapts the Time-Dependent Variational Principle (TDVP) to map the non-unitary ITE operator onto parameterized quantum circuits (PQC) using techniques like ancilla-assisted embedding.
model_or_system: The primary physical system is an infinite 1D quantum chain, benchmarked using the transverse-field Ising model. The quantum state is represented by uniform Matrix Product States (uMPSs).
key_observables: Ground-state energy estimate, cost function distribution, energy density distribution, and the ratio of parameter variance to shot noise variance.
important_parameters: Bond dimension (D=2), number of shots ($N_{	ext{shots}}$), and the time step ($	au$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes translational invariance (uMPS ansatz) and relies on approximations for the non-unitary evolution operator (e.g., unitary embedding or unitary approximation).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the mapping of cost functions to quantum circuits, compare energy estimates from different methods (QLanczos vs. QITE), and show the statistical comparison of energy fluctuations against theoretical distributions.
paper_structure: The paper first reviews TDVP for real-time evolution, then details the quantum-circuit TDVP framework for ITE on infinite systems, followed by detailed analyses of energy estimation refinement using QLanczos and statistical characterization of noise in optimization landscapes.
why_interesting: It provides concrete, implementable quantum algorithms for simulating ground-state properties of 1D quantum systems, directly bridging advanced quantum simulation techniques (MPS, TDVP) with NISQ hardware constraints (noise analysis).
